2 and FBe  (2e)(1ZBe)> rBe 2 . The internuclear repulsive force always opposes formation of a chemical bond (Fig. 3.14a), so we must identify some force that overcomes this repulsion. We need only consider the attractive forces and ask, “Over what region in space does the electron exert forces on the nuclei that will tend to pull them together?” Only the component of the attractive force directed along the internuclear axis is effective in drawing them together. Clearly, for all posi- tions of the electron “between” the nuclei (for example, see Fig. 3.14b), the forces

FAe 9 and FBe 9 will tend to pull the nuclei together. In contrast, when the electron is “outside” the internuclear region (for example, see Fig. 3.14c), it exerts a greater force on the nearer nucleus than the farther, pulling the nuclei apart.
